name: Nasco di Cagliari

climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.
Carignano is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 5°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
